newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-GLOBAL CHALLENGE YACHTS LEAVE AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-GLOBAL CHALLENGE YACHTS LEAVE AUSTRALIA.

text.p: The 14 contenders in the gruelling around-the-world BT Global Challenge yacht race left Sydney on Sunday after a controversial start to the event's fourth leg, race officials said.
The yacht Save the Children was the early leader after the start of the 6,300-nautical mile leg from Sydney to Cape Town.
Officials said 10 protests had been lodged after the yacht Commercial Union overshot the starting line in Sydney Harbour and was later involved in a minor collision with overall race leader, Group 4.
Commercial Union was in second place shortly after the start with Group 4 back in eighth. Save the Children won the previous leg from Wellington in New Zealand to Sydney.

All crews in the challenge, considered one of the world's toughest around-the-world sailing races because it goes against prevailing winds, are amateurs who paid about A$40,000 (US$30,800) each to take part.
The skippers of the 20-metre (yard) steel-built yachts are professionals.
The race, which started last September, takes the boats 48,000 km from Southampton, England, around the world via South America, New Zealand, Australia and Africa.
The yachts should take about 40 days to reach Cape Town and are expected to arrive back in Southampton around July.
